newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AHK to up weekly ex-Europe flights to 9 from four.
newsitem.headline: AHK to up weekly ex-Europe flights to 9 from four.

text.p: Air Hong Kong will increase its ex-Europe frequencies to nine from the present four times a week in August, said the all-cargo carrier's European general manager, Marcel Buelens.
The airline, 75 percent owned by Cathay Pacific Airways, will raise its weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter flights on the route to five from four next week.
Then it hopes to gradually increase the frequency to daily in July, all connecting the carrier's European hubs of Brussels and Manchester, he said.
In August, two more flights will be introduced to boost the total to nine. These two are likely to be on Thursdays and Sundays, respectively direct from Brussels and from Manchester, he said.
Buelens added that the forthcoming operation of nine weekly flights had also led AHK to consider developing a southern European hub.
Italy and Spain are being considered and the move would be in joint co-operation with a major European airline or airlines, which Buelens declined to name.
"A third hub would be used to support the nine flights. Spain is being seriously considered," he said.
"In the past we have let our customers down (by providing them with insufficient) capacity. But we want to say that the capacity is here to stay," he stressed.
He added all of the major integrators were customers of the airline.
Currently, the Europe-Hong Kong market is booming, he said, and AHK was having to turn down cargo each day.
AHK also expected the European-Hong Kong market to expand even more in the summer when Hong Kong is handed back to China, said Buelens.
The carrier currently operates three 747-200 freighters.
